analyst_view.overall: Eibar are fourth but have not played since a 1-1 draw with Almería on 31 October, after their trip to Castellón was postponed, and have one league win in their last five. Cádiz are 20th and have lost two in a row under Borja Jiménez, the latest 1-2 at home to Oviedo with a late Urko Izeta header. I found little fresh team news this week, so the view rests mainly on form and LaLiga's season figures; no referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I have moved from lower to same: Eibar keep games tight with little of the ball, but their league games average close to three goals (21-14 in 12) and Cádiz's about two and a half. The site's figure already sits below both teams' averages.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, with 5.4 for Eibar. I lean slightly lower: Eibar pass less than most (4,806 passes in 12 games by LaLiga's count) and rarely build the sustained pressure that wins corners, even at home.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. I lean higher: LaLiga has Cádiz on 42 yellows in 13 games, and a side in the relegation zone after two defeats will have to fight for every second ball. Jokin Aranbarri has also asked his players to be more aggressive, so Eibar's 1.9 looks low.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with 17.5 for Eibar. That looks high: LaLiga counts Eibar at 121 shots in 12 games and Cádiz at 111 in 13, both around ten a game or fewer. Two weeks without a league game adds to the case for a slower match.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean lower in line with the shots: Eibar scored one goal or none in each of their last three league games, and Cádiz have been blunt away. Antoñito is Cádiz's top scorer with five.
